[latex]\dot{x}=Ax+Bu[/latex],
[latex]y=Cx[/latex]

where [latex]x[/latex] is state vector, u is input, y is output and [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 0 &-2 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], [latex]B=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], [latex]C=[1 \; \; 0][/latex]

A unity feedback is provided to the above system G(s) to make it a closed loop system as shown in figure.

explanation_text: [latex]G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+2)} [/latex] and  [latex] H(s)=1[/latex] [latex] r(t)=u(t) [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; R(s)=\frac{1}{s} [/latex] [latex]Error=E(s)=\frac{R(s)}{1+G(s)H(s)} [/latex] [latex]\;\;=\frac{\frac{1}{s}}{1+\frac{1}{s(s+2)}} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; E(s)=\frac{s+2}{s(s+2)+1} [/latex] Steady state error, using final value theorem [latex]e_{ss}=\lim{s\rightarrow 0}sE(s) [/latex] [latex]\;\;\lim{s\rightarrow 0}\frac{s(s+2)}{s(s+2)+1}=0[/latex]
explanation_html:
[latex]G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s+2)} [/latex]
and [latex] H(s)=1[/latex]
[latex] r(t)=u(t) [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; R(s)=\frac{1}{s} [/latex]
[latex]Error=E(s)=\frac{R(s)}{1+G(s)H(s)} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;=\frac{\frac{1}{s}}{1+\frac{1}{s(s+2)}} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; E(s)=\frac{s+2}{s(s+2)+1} [/latex]
Steady state error, using final value theorem
[latex]e_{ss}=\lim{s\rightarrow 0}sE(s) [/latex]
[latex]\;\;\lim{s\rightarrow 0}\frac{s(s+2)}{s(s+2)+1}=0[/latex]

subject: Electrical Machines - DC Machines
explanation_text: Before plugging Current through field winding, [latex]\begin{aligned} I_f &=\frac{V_t}{R_f} =\frac{240}{80}=3A\\ I_L &=I_f+I_a \end{aligned}[/latex] Current through armature [latex]\begin{aligned} I_a &=I_L-I_f\\ &= 15-3=12A\\ \text{Back emf}&=E_a=V_t-I_aR_a\\ &=240-12 \times 0.5\\ &=234V \end{aligned}[/latex]In plugging, the connection of armature winding is reversed. A strong baking torque is achieved by maintaining the supply voltage to the armature with connections reversed. So, the net voltage across the armature resistance at the time of plugging [latex]E_a+V=240+234=474V[/latex]
